subject.title: [Feature]: First-class multi-instance management for Docker installs

question: Should OpenClaw core own first-class Docker instance create/list/delete/update commands, or should multi-instance Docker remain a documented manual Compose/profile workflow for now?
rationale: This is a new official operator UX and persistent lifecycle contract across Docker, Compose, ports, state roots, workspaces, deletion, updates, and sandbox boundaries, so automation should not choose the product boundary.

options.title: Define minimal core lifecycle
options.body: Approve a narrow core-owned Docker instance lifecycle with explicit persistence, ports, update/delete, and security semantics before implementation.

options.title: Keep manual primitives
options.body: Continue documenting profile, env, and Compose isolation as the supported path and close or defer this broader lifecycle ask.

options.title: Route to wrapper/plugin
options.body: Keep core lean and sponsor an external ClawHub or wrapper workflow unless it exposes a missing core API.

recommendation.title: Define minimal core lifecycle
recommendation.body: Approve a narrow core-owned Docker instance lifecycle with explicit persistence, ports, update/delete, and security semantics before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The most relevant prior history is around multi-gateway docs and profile-aware service naming, which are central to this product decision.
